subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Leaning Tower of Pisa usable.

hook.text: The Tower of Pisa started leaning during construction in 1178 — and never stopped.

buildup.text: One side sits on softer clay than the other. Differential settlement caused the tilt.

discovery.text: Construction paused for 100 years. During that pause, the clay strengthened under load.

twist.text: In the 1990s, engineers extracted soil from the high side to gently reduce the lean.

climax.text: They straightened it by 18 inches — enough to last another 200 years.

punchline.text: The world's most famous mistake taught us how soil behaves.

quiz.question: How did engineers reduce the Tower of Pisa's lean in the 1990s?
options: They added heavy weights to the high side of the tower
They carefully extracted soil from beneath the high side
They rebuilt the foundation entirely using modern concrete
